observations.interpretation: The runner explicitly moved /workspace to a unique WA-023 branch before research.
After OBS-WA-023-02 and without this runner switching /workspace again, the same toplevel reported a second other unit's branch.
A linked worktree created as a fail-closed fallback retained the WA-023 branch and a distinct toplevel.

outcome_basis: OBS-WA-023-01 and OBS-WA-023-03 show that the assigned /workspace checkout was shared across unit branches rather than isolated for this best-of-N runner.
OBS-WA-023-04 shows that the underlying Git linked-worktree mechanism can restore checkout-level isolation when a distinct toplevel is actually allocated.
scope_limit: The observations refute this run's assigned checkout isolation. They do not establish a defect in every Cursor worktree route or version.
